qs.q: An investigator studies an enzyme-catalyzed reaction and observes that maximum velocity increases when an activator molecule binds to a non-active site. What type of allosteric regulation is occurring?
o: K system allosteric activation altering substrate affinity without changing Vmax
V system allosteric activation increasing catalytic turnover rate parameters
Covalent modification phosphorylation enhancing intrinsic enzymatic activity
Feedback inhibition slowing down upstream metabolic pathway production rates
Zymogen cleavage exposing hidden catalytic pockets for substrate binding
qs.e: In V-system allosteric enzymes, the activator increases Vmax without necessarily affecting the apparent Km.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Biochemistry Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Allosteric regulation of an enzyme typically involves:
o: D. Enzyme amount changes via synthesis or degradation
C. Molecule occupies the active site, blocking substrate entry
B. Enzyme undergoes covalent modification such as phosphorylation
A. Effector binds away from the active site, altering enzyme shape
qs.e: Allosteric regulation involves the binding of an effector molecule to an allosteric site (a site distinct from the active site) on the enzyme. This binding induces a conformational change that affects the enzyme's activity, either activating or inhibiting it.
